title: Definition has no eval coverage
description: Eval coverage lets you compare authored AI behavior against known cases and catch regressions before prompts, agents, flows, or pipelines drift.
rationale: Eval coverage lets you compare authored AI behavior against known cases and catch regressions before prompts, agents, flows, or pipelines drift.
impact: Uncovered definitions can regress silently when prompts, models, tools, or orchestration logic changes.

fixes.title: Add eval coverage
fixes.description: Add an Eval that covers this definition so regressions can be detected.

title: Agent handoff target is not index-visible
description: Index-visible handoff targets let you inspect the handoff path, connect parent and delegated work, and trust the trace tree when agents transfer control.
rationale: Index-visible handoff targets let you inspect the handoff path, connect parent and delegated work, and trust the trace tree when agents transfer control.
impact: A handoff to an unindexed or missing agent can appear as an orphaned tool call, missing branch, or disconnected trace segment.

fixes.title: Make the handoff target visible
fixes.description: Define and export the target agent with a stable id, or update the handoff id so it points at a index-visible agent.

title: Prompt has no input schema
description: Prompt input schemas are the TypeScript contract for prompt inputs, context joins, replay, eval cases, and devtools inspection.
rationale: Prompt input schemas are the TypeScript contract for prompt inputs, context joins, replay, eval cases, and devtools inspection.
impact: Untyped prompt inputs are harder to validate, replay, compare, and safely refactor as the prompt evolves.

fixes.title: Declare prompt input
fixes.description: Add an input schema to the prompt so calls, eval cases, and traces share one inspectable contract.

title: Prompt has no output schema
description: Prompt output schemas make generated objects inspectable and comparable, and let evals assert structured behavior instead of only text.
rationale: Prompt output schemas make generated objects inspectable and comparable, and let evals assert structured behavior instead of only text.
impact: Unstructured prompt outputs can make downstream code, replay, and regression checks depend on ad hoc parsing.

fixes.title: Declare prompt output
fixes.description: Add an output schema when this prompt is expected to produce structured data or feed downstream logic.

title: Prompt has injected required input
description: Injected contexts and injectables can make a prompt require fields that are not visible in the prompt authored input schema. Surfacing those fields keeps prompt calls, eval cases, and replay inputs honest.
rationale: Injected contexts and injectables can make a prompt require fields that are not visible in the prompt authored input schema. Surfacing those fields keeps prompt calls, eval cases, and replay inputs honest.
impact: Callers can miss a required field because the requirement is hidden behind prompt composition instead of declared on the prompt itself.

fixes.title: Make the requirement visible
fixes.description: Either add the field to the prompt input schema, make the injected source optional, or document why the injected requirement is intentionally hidden.

title: Prompt has conflicting injected input
description: When multiple injected sources contribute the same input field with obviously incompatible schemas, callers and eval cases cannot know which contract is authoritative.
rationale: When multiple injected sources contribute the same input field with obviously incompatible schemas, callers and eval cases cannot know which contract is authoritative.
impact: Prompt calls can validate differently depending on composition order, and generated devtools or replay forms may show a misleading contract.

fixes.title: Align contributed schemas
fixes.description: Rename one field, make the schemas compatible, or move the shared field into the prompt input schema so every injected source agrees on the contract.

title: Prompt has conditionally required input
description: A field required by an injected source becomes only conditionally required when the source is guarded by when, match, or runtime-dependent composition. The global prompt schema must keep it optional, but authors still need to know which branch needs it.
rationale: A field required by an injected source becomes only conditionally required when the source is guarded by when, match, or runtime-dependent composition. The global prompt schema must keep it optional, but authors still need to know which branch needs it.
impact: Eval cases and callers can miss branch-specific input unless the conditional requirement is visible in the Project Index.

fixes.title: Document the branch requirement
fixes.description: Keep the global field optional, but document or model the branch where it is required. If the branch always runs, remove the conditional wrapper.

title: Dynamic context has no resolved input schema
description: Context input schemas make conditional and dynamic context injection explicit, inspectable, and type-safe across prompt composition.
rationale: Context input schemas make conditional and dynamic context injection explicit, inspectable, and type-safe across prompt composition.
impact: Dynamic context without a resolved input contract can hide missing fields until runtime and make context windows harder to debug.

fixes.title: Declare resolvable context input
fixes.description: Use an inline or import-safe schema for the context input so Crux can project the contract into the index.

title: Injection dependency is runtime-dependent
description: Runtime-dependent injection is allowed, but the Project Index cannot fully explain the prompt or context graph from source alone. Marking the dynamic edge makes that blind spot visible.
rationale: Runtime-dependent injection is allowed, but the Project Index cannot fully explain the prompt or context graph from source alone. Marking the dynamic edge makes that blind spot visible.
impact: Devtools, eval coverage, and static linting may under-report the contexts, memory, or injectables that can affect this definition.

fixes.title: Declare static use when possible
fixes.description: Move stable dependencies into a static use array or keep the dynamic path intentional and documented with a suppression reason.

title: Injected tools are runtime-dependent
description: Contexts and injectables can contribute tools dynamically. That keeps authoring flexible, but it means the model-facing tool surface cannot be fully inspected from static source.
rationale: Contexts and injectables can contribute tools dynamically. That keeps authoring flexible, but it means the model-facing tool surface cannot be fully inspected from static source.
impact: A prompt or context may gain tools that are absent from the static Project Index, making safety review, replay, and eval setup less precise.

fixes.title: Expose stable tool names
fixes.description: Prefer static tool maps or named tool contributors where possible. Suppress only when the runtime-selected tool set is intentional.

title: Prompt receives tools through injection
description: Tools can enter a prompt through contexts and injectables rather than the prompt body itself. Surfacing that indirect tool surface makes safety review, eval setup, and replay easier to reason about.
rationale: Tools can enter a prompt through contexts and injectables rather than the prompt body itself. Surfacing that indirect tool surface makes safety review, eval setup, and replay easier to reason about.
impact: Authors can miss model-facing tools because the prompt does not declare them directly, especially when the tool source is multiple injection hops away.

fixes.title: Review the indirect tool source
fixes.description: Keep the indirect tool surface intentional, document the injected source, or move stable tools closer to the prompt when direct visibility matters.

title: Injectable is not used by the indexed graph
description: An index-visible injectable that is never reached from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or a dynamically consumed dependency the static graph cannot see.
rationale: An index-visible injectable that is never reached from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or a dynamically consumed dependency the static graph cannot see.
impact: Unused injectables can make prompt composition harder to scan and can hide stale schema or tool contracts.

fixes.title: Use, remove, or suppress
fixes.description: Wire the injectable into a static use path, remove it if it is stale, or suppress the finding when it is intentionally consumed dynamically or externally.

title: Context is not used by the indexed graph
description: A context that is not reachable from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or may only be selected through dynamic runtime composition.
rationale: A context that is not reachable from any prompt, context, or injectable may be dead authoring surface or may only be selected through dynamic runtime composition.
impact: Unused contexts can keep stale prompt text, schema requirements, or tool surfaces alive without clear consumers.

fixes.title: Use, remove, or suppress
fixes.description: Wire the context into a static use path, remove it if it is stale, or suppress the finding when dynamic or external composition is intentional.

title: Injection target is unresolved
description: A static-looking use entry that cannot be resolved to an index-visible definition makes the injection graph incomplete and can hide schema, tools, memory, or prompt text.
rationale: A static-looking use entry that cannot be resolved to an index-visible definition makes the injection graph incomplete and can hide schema, tools, memory, or prompt text.
impact: Devtools and lints may under-report what affects the prompt or context because a visible use target could not be linked.

fixes.title: Make the target resolvable
fixes.description: Export or inline the target definition, avoid opaque aliases for static use entries, or intentionally mark the dependency as dynamic.

title: Injected input comes from a deep chain
description: Deeply injected schema requirements are harder to discover from the prompt surface and harder to keep aligned with callers and eval cases.
rationale: Deeply injected schema requirements are harder to discover from the prompt surface and harder to keep aligned with callers and eval cases.
impact: A prompt can appear simple while relying on fields contributed several composition hops away, making refactors and replay setup more fragile.

fixes.title: Flatten or document the chain
fixes.description: Move important input requirements closer to the prompt, reduce composition depth, or document why the deep injection path is intentional.

title: Flow args are not inspectable
description: Flow argument schemas document the durable or immediate entry contract and make flow starts, resumes, and eval cases inspectable.
rationale: Flow argument schemas document the durable or immediate entry contract and make flow starts, resumes, and eval cases inspectable.
impact: Untyped flow arguments can make resumed work and flow evals depend on undocumented input shapes.

fixes.title: Declare flow args
fixes.description: Add an import-safe args schema or Convex validator object so Crux can project the flow input contract.

title: Tool has no input schema
description: Tool input schemas make model-emitted arguments inspectable, validateable, and easier for your team to debug across traces, evals, and generated devtools UI.
rationale: Tool input schemas make model-emitted arguments inspectable, validateable, and easier for your team to debug across traces, evals, and generated devtools UI.
impact: Untyped tool calls are harder to validate, inspect, replay, and explain when an agent makes a bad call.

fixes.title: Declare tool parameters
fixes.description: Add a Zod or JSON-schema-compatible input schema to the tool parameters so arguments are validated and inspectable.

title: Tool output is not model-inspectable
description: A model-output adapter makes tool results explicit for traces, replay, and debugging the model intent-to-execution chain.
rationale: A model-output adapter makes tool results explicit for traces, replay, and debugging the model intent-to-execution chain.
impact: Raw tool outputs can be hard to inspect or compare when the application result differs from what the model receives.

fixes.title: Declare model output mapping
fixes.description: Add a toModelOutput adapter when the tool result needs a stable, inspectable model-facing representation.

title: Suspending flow has no eval coverage
description: Suspension paths cross time, approval, and runtime boundaries, so you need regression coverage for resume behavior and stale pending work.
rationale: Suspension paths cross time, approval, and runtime boundaries, so you need regression coverage for resume behavior and stale pending work.
impact: A broken suspend/resume path can strand user work or continue with stale state after approval.

fixes.title: Cover suspend and resume
fixes.description: Add a flow eval that exercises the suspend/resume path, including the expected approval or signal.

title: Flow repeats a step label
description: Flow step labels are durable replay identities. Repeating a label in one flow body makes cached output ambiguous across retries, suspension, and resume.
rationale: Flow step labels are durable replay identities. Repeating a label in one flow body makes cached output ambiguous across retries, suspension, and resume.
impact: A repeated step label can return the wrong cached output or fail at runtime before the flow reaches later work.

fixes.title: Use unique step labels
fixes.description: Give each flow.step() call a distinct literal label, and encode loop iteration or branch meaning in the label only when it is stable across resumes.

title: Flow repeats a suspend name
description: Flow signal delivery is keyed by signal name and consumed after one delivery. Repeating a suspend name in one flow body makes later resumes depend on source-order replay rather than a distinct signal contract.
rationale: Flow signal delivery is keyed by signal name and consumed after one delivery. Repeating a suspend name in one flow body makes later resumes depend on source-order replay rather than a distinct signal contract.
impact: A repeated suspend name can make approvals ambiguous and can strand a later wait behind an already-used signal name.

fixes.title: Use unique suspend names
fixes.description: Give each suspend point a distinct literal name, or split repeated waits into separate flows until scoped/repeating signal attempts are supported.

title: Flow suspends on an undeclared signal
description: A local signal map is the public signal contract for a flow. Literal suspend names outside that map cannot be signaled through the typed handle and usually mean the runtime contract drifted from the authored type contract.
rationale: A local signal map is the public signal contract for a flow. Literal suspend names outside that map cannot be signaled through the typed handle and usually mean the runtime contract drifted from the authored type contract.
impact: A flow may suspend at a signal that callers cannot discover or type-check through the flow handle.

fixes.title: Declare or rename the signal
fixes.description: Add the suspend name to the flow signals map, or rename the suspend call to one of the declared signal keys.

title: Writable workspace has no guardrail
description: Writable workspaces can mutate drafts, files, and artifacts; guardrails help you keep those mutations policy-checked, auditable, and observable.
rationale: Writable workspaces can mutate drafts, files, and artifacts; guardrails help you keep those mutations policy-checked, auditable, and observable.
impact: Unprotected workspace writes can damage user content or make file mutations difficult to audit after the fact.

fixes.title: Attach a guardrail
fixes.description: Attach a guardrail to the workspace or its write/delete tools so mutations are inspectable and policy-checked.

title: Effect identity is defined more than once
description: Distinct effect() call sites declare the same literal id and version.
rationale: Effect receipt and recovery identity is the (id, version) pair and must resolve to one definition.
impact: Runtime registration rejects conflicting definitions and Catalog/runtime joins become ambiguous.

fixes.title: Make the Effect identity unique
fixes.description: Change the id or version, or re-export the existing Effect definition instead of calling effect() again.

title: Irreversible Effect is inside a required-recovery boundary
description: A statically identified Effect with no recovery is called inside a statically required rollbackOnError() boundary.
rationale: A required-recovery boundary promises that every contained Effect can be recovered, and the strict default must teach every valid escape hatch.
impact: The required boundary blocks the irreversible Effect before mutation, so the authored operation cannot proceed as written.

fixes.title: Define recovery
fixes.description: Add a recovery handler to the Effect definition.

fixes.title: Move the Effect outside
fixes.description: Call the irreversible Effect outside the required-recovery boundary.

fixes.title: Choose best-effort recovery
fixes.description: Set the boundary option to { recovery: 'best-effort' } when partial rollback is acceptable.

title: Safety policy id is duplicated
description: Safety policy ids are used in decisions, traces, Project Index rows, and test matchers. Reusing an id makes it hard to tell which policy blocked, rewrote, or retried a turn.
rationale: Safety policy ids are used in decisions, traces, Project Index rows, and test matchers. Reusing an id makes it hard to tell which policy blocked, rewrote, or retried a turn.
impact: Duplicate policy ids can make Devtools, observability, and Eval assertions point at the wrong safety policy.

fixes.title: Rename one policy
fixes.description: Give each guardrail, constraint, and tool policy a unique id within the project safety surface.

title: Session construction is ambiguous
description: Canonical Session creation uses session(agent, { key }) and keyed lookup uses getSession(agent, key), with exactly the supported arguments.
rationale: Canonical Session creation uses session(agent, { key }) and keyed lookup uses getSession(agent, key), with exactly the supported arguments.
impact: An indirect options object or unexpected arity can hide immutable identity inputs and prevent tooling from proving what durable Session is addressed.

fixes.title: Use the canonical Session call
fixes.description: Pass exactly one Agent and an inline options object with key to session(), or one Agent and key to getSession().

title: Session target is not a static Agent or Flow
description: A durable Session target must resolve to one authored Agent or Flow definition that generated runtime artifacts can import in a later process.
rationale: A durable Session target must resolve to one authored Agent or Flow definition that generated runtime artifacts can import in a later process.
impact: An unresolved or runtime-selected target cannot be pinned to one durable definition fingerprint and may fail when the Session wakes.

fixes.title: Pass one static Agent or Flow target
fixes.description: Pass a top-level local or imported Agent or Flow definition directly instead of selecting or constructing the target dynamically.

title: Session Thread view is mutated outside its owner
description: A Session exposes a read-only Thread view. Only the Session owner may publish canonical history through the owner-checked linearizable mutation path.
rationale: A Session exposes a read-only Thread view. Only the Session owner may publish canonical history through the owner-checked linearizable mutation path.
impact: Calling a mutating Thread method through the Session view is rejected by owner enforcement and cannot safely update the Session conversation.

fixes.title: Send input through the Session
fixes.description: Use session.send() or session.sendMany(); keep session.thread for read-only inspection.

title: Session Agent binds a shared concrete Thread
description: Each durable Session owns its own canonical Thread. An Agent used as a Session target should not also bind a concrete authored Thread shared by every Session instance.
rationale: Each durable Session owns its own canonical Thread. An Agent used as a Session target should not also bind a concrete authored Thread shared by every Session instance.
impact: Different Session keys can read shared conversation history through the Agent binding, breaking the expected tenant boundary even though their owned Thread heads remain distinct.

fixes.title: Use the Session-owned Thread
fixes.description: Remove the concrete Thread from the Session Agent use graph and let each Session supply its owner-scoped history.

title: Session identity is not stable
description: Durable Agent Sessions require a statically provable target and caller key so generated runtime artifacts and later processes address the same owner.
rationale: Durable Agent Sessions require a statically provable target and caller key so generated runtime artifacts and later processes address the same owner.
impact: A dynamic key can create a different Session or make the intended durable identity invisible to tooling and deployment checks.

fixes.title: Use a stable Session key
fixes.description: Pass a direct caller-controlled string literal as the Session key and keep the Agent target statically resolvable.

title: Definition resolves multiple Thread bindings
description: A prompt or agent can bind one canonical Thread history. Resolving multiple Thread targets makes the history source and accepted-turn commit destination ambiguous.
rationale: A prompt or agent can bind one canonical Thread history. Resolving multiple Thread targets makes the history source and accepted-turn commit destination ambiguous.
impact: Conflicting Thread bindings can make managed execution read from or publish accepted turns to an unintended conversation tree.

fixes.title: Keep one Thread binding
fixes.description: Remove the extra Thread entry from the prompt or agent use graph so managed execution resolves exactly one canonical history.

title: Thread id is active more than once
description: Active Thread ids identify one canonical conversation tree. Reusing an id in multiple active definitions makes storage, runtime evidence, and developer tooling point at an ambiguous Thread.
rationale: Active Thread ids identify one canonical conversation tree. Reusing an id in multiple active definitions makes storage, runtime evidence, and developer tooling point at an ambiguous Thread.
impact: Duplicate active Thread ids can make unrelated definitions share canonical history or attach tooling to the wrong authored source.

fixes.title: Give each active Thread a unique id
fixes.description: Rename one thread() id or remove the duplicate active export so each canonical conversation tree has one authored identity.

title: Long-lived memory has no retention policy
description: Long-lived episodic and semantic memory can accumulate stale or sensitive facts; a retention policy makes lifetime and cleanup behavior explicit.
rationale: Long-lived episodic and semantic memory can accumulate stale or sensitive facts; a retention policy makes lifetime and cleanup behavior explicit.
impact: Memory without a visible retention policy can silently grow, preserve stale context, or keep user data longer than intended.

fixes.title: Declare memory retention
fixes.description: Add an eviction or retention policy to long-lived memory so cleanup behavior is inspectable.

title: State resource is written but never read
description: A memory, blackboard, or workspace that receives writes but has no visible read path can indicate unreachable context, forgotten state, or an output-only side effect that should be intentional.
rationale: A memory, blackboard, or workspace that receives writes but has no visible read path can indicate unreachable context, forgotten state, or an output-only side effect that should be intentional.
impact: Written-but-unread state can make agents appear to remember or persist work that is never actually used by prompts, tools, flows, or later runs.

fixes.title: Connect or document the read path
fixes.description: Add a index-visible read path for this resource, or suppress the rule with a reason when the write is intentionally output-only.

title: Consensus has no visible judge or scorer
description: Consensus compositions need an inspectable decision policy so users can understand why one answer, plan, or agent output won.
rationale: Consensus compositions need an inspectable decision policy so users can understand why one answer, plan, or agent output won.
impact: Without a visible judge or scorer, consensus behavior can look arbitrary in traces and may be hard to test or tune.

fixes.title: Attach a judge or scorer
fixes.description: Add a index-visible judge agent or scorer to the consensus composition so the decision policy is inspectable.

title: Shared blackboard has no conflict policy
description: Shared blackboards can receive writes from multiple agents; a conflict policy helps your team understand and debug merge behavior.
rationale: Shared blackboards can receive writes from multiple agents; a conflict policy helps your team understand and debug merge behavior.
impact: Concurrent agent writes can overwrite or contradict each other without an explicit policy for resolving shared state.

fixes.title: Declare a conflict policy
fixes.description: Declare a blackboard conflict policy, such as consensus, judge, or last-writer-wins, when multiple agents can write shared state.

title: Routing primitive has no stable id
description: Stable routing ids let index definitions, route decision spans, and Eval history join reliably even when variables or files are renamed.
rationale: Stable routing ids let index definitions, route decision spans, and Eval history join reliably even when variables or files are renamed.
impact: Routes can still be indexed from variable names, but runtime joins and historical comparisons are less durable across refactors.

fixes.title: Add a routing id
fixes.description: Add id to router(), split(), retry(), cascade(), or fallback() options so authored routing and runtime spans share a stable join key.

title: Router has no default route
description: Routers need an explicit default route so unknown classifier outputs remain observable and deterministic instead of failing or silently depending on adapter behavior.
rationale: Routers need an explicit default route so unknown classifier outputs remain observable and deterministic instead of failing or silently depending on adapter behavior.
impact: A classifier returning an unexpected key can produce confusing route decisions and incomplete route coverage in traces.

fixes.title: Add default route
fixes.description: Add a default entry to the router routes map and point it at the safest fallback model or policy.

title: Routing target is not index-visible
description: Route, split route, retry target, tier, and fallback option targets should connect to index-visible agents, prompts, or nested routing primitives so users can inspect the authored decision graph.
rationale: Route, split route, retry target, tier, and fallback option targets should connect to index-visible agents, prompts, or nested routing primitives so users can inspect the authored decision graph.
impact: Unresolved route targets appear as plain model references, which limits architecture views, impact analysis, and runtime span joins.

fixes.title: Make target visible
fixes.description: Reference an exported Crux definition or routing primitive, or keep raw model targets intentional and suppress this rule with a reason.

title: Cascade tier makes later tiers unreachable
description: A cascade tier without an evaluator accepts by default, so any following tiers are never reached unless that tier throws.
rationale: A cascade tier without an evaluator accepts by default, so any following tiers are never reached unless that tier throws.
impact: Expensive backup tiers may look configured but never run, making quality escalation and cost expectations misleading.

fixes.title: Add evaluator or reorder tiers
fixes.description: Add evaluate to non-terminal tiers, or move unconditional accept tiers to the end of the cascade.

title: RAG recipe step target is unresolved
description: Recipe steps are only explainable in devtools when retriever, scorer, and reranker targets resolve to indexed definitions.
rationale: Recipe steps are only explainable in devtools when retriever, scorer, and reranker targets resolve to indexed definitions.
impact: The recipe may still run, but the Project Index cannot show or validate the step dependency that authored code appears to reference.

fixes.title: Export or define the step target
fixes.description: Reference an indexed retriever, scorer, or reranker definition from the recipe step, or suppress this rule if the dependency is intentionally external.

title: Relation expansion selects an unknown type
description: expandRelations({ types }) should name relation types declared by the Connected Knowledge relation vocabulary visible to the recipe.
rationale: expandRelations({ types }) should name relation types declared by the Connected Knowledge relation vocabulary visible to the recipe.
impact: Unknown relation selections make graph expansion narrower than authored code suggests and can hide missing connected-knowledge coverage.

fixes.title: Use a declared relation type
fixes.description: Rename the selected type or add it to the relation vocabulary in the knowledge pipeline.

title: Knowledge recipe has multiple producer steps
description: Connected Knowledge recipes must choose exactly one producer step, either retrieve() or globalSearch().
rationale: Connected Knowledge recipes must choose exactly one producer step, either retrieve() or globalSearch().
impact: Multiple producers make recipe execution ambiguous and mirror a runtime failure before retrieval can produce hits.

fixes.title: Keep one producer step
fixes.description: Remove the duplicate retrieve() or globalSearch() step so the recipe has exactly one producer.

title: Assertion selection names an unknown type
description: knowledgeBase().assertions(stage, { types }) and view.assertions(stage, { types }) should select assertion types declared by the stage.
rationale: knowledgeBase().assertions(stage, { types }) and view.assertions(stage, { types }) should select assertion types declared by the stage.
impact: Unknown assertion selections produce empty or incomplete assertion context even though authored code appears to request a typed subset.

fixes.title: Use a declared assertion type
fixes.description: Rename the selected assertion type or add it to the assertion stage types map.

title: Runtime target name is duplicated
description: Durable runtime target names are persisted as routing identities. Each flow or durable task name must resolve to exactly one target so resumed work wakes the intended code.
rationale: Durable runtime target names are persisted as routing identities. Each flow or durable task name must resolve to exactly one target so resumed work wakes the intended code.
impact: Duplicate target names make generated runtime artifacts ambiguous and can block or misroute pending durable work.

fixes.title: Rename one runtime target
fixes.description: Give each flow() or durableTask() declaration a distinct literal name, then run crux runtime generate.

title: Runtime target name is not literal
description: Runtime artifacts need a durable target name that can be discovered before deployment. Dynamic names cannot be matched to pending work in a fresh process.
rationale: Runtime artifacts need a durable target name that can be discovered before deployment. Dynamic names cannot be matched to pending work in a fresh process.
impact: Generated manifests cannot safely include the target, so future wakes may fail with TARGET_NOT_FOUND.

fixes.title: Use a literal durable name
fixes.description: Change flow(name, ...) or durableTask(name, ...) to a literal string name and regenerate runtime artifacts.

title: Runtime target is not exported
description: Serverless and host-bound runtime entries import targets by named export. Local or nested targets cannot be woken in a later process.
rationale: Serverless and host-bound runtime entries import targets by named export. Local or nested targets cannot be woken in a later process.
impact: The target is visible to local analysis but cannot be wired into generated runtime entry files.

fixes.title: Export the target declaration
fixes.description: Move the target to a top-level exported const/function declaration, then run crux runtime generate.

title: Durable defer target is an inline closure
description: Durable background work must name a durable task target so Crux can import and wake it in a later process. Inline closures are request-scoped code, not durable targets.
rationale: Durable background work must name a durable task target so Crux can import and wake it in a later process. Inline closures are request-scoped code, not durable targets.
impact: The deferred work cannot be represented in generated runtime artifacts or resumed after process exit.

fixes.title: Use a named durable task
fixes.description: Move the closure into an exported durableTask() from @use-crux/core/runtime, or use request-scoped defer(callback) when RFC #135 lands.

title: Public defer used in replayable code
description: Public defer() is invocation-scoped and cannot be replayed safely inside a flow body or step.
rationale: A replay could schedule the same request-scoped or durable work more than once.
impact: Replayed execution can duplicate background work.

fixes.title: Use flow.defer
fixes.description: Schedule replay-safe durable work through flow.defer().

title: Named defer promise is not consumed
description: Named defer() must be awaited, returned, or included in recognized promise composition.
rationale: The promise is the durable commit barrier for the scheduled intent.
impact: The host may commit before durable scheduling has succeeded.

fixes.title: Await the promise
fixes.description: Await or return the named defer() promise.

title: Runtime-bound API used without runtime config
description: Name-bound, time-bound, event-bound, and background APIs need a configured Runtime Engine. Without one, only object-bound flow APIs can keep working.
rationale: Name-bound, time-bound, event-bound, and background APIs need a configured Runtime Engine. Without one, only object-bound flow APIs can keep working.
impact: The API will throw RUNTIME_REQUIRED when it executes in a project without runtime configuration.

fixes.title: Configure a runtime
fixes.description: Add a runtime entry to crux.config.ts, for example runtime: node() for local development.

title: Flow body contains nondeterministic code
description: Flow bodies can replay after suspension. Calls like Date.now() and Math.random() outside flow.step() can produce different replay fingerprints or decisions.
rationale: Flow bodies can replay after suspension. Calls like Date.now() and Math.random() outside flow.step() can produce different replay fingerprints or decisions.
impact: A resumed flow may diverge from its original execution or block with REPLAY_DIVERGED.

fixes.title: Move nondeterminism into a step
fixes.description: Wrap nondeterministic reads in flow.step() so the first value is cached and replay can reuse it.

title: Durable runtime payload is not JSON-serializable
description: Durable runtime boundaries persist payloads as JSON so they can be replayed, inspected, and delivered across adapters.
rationale: Durable runtime boundaries persist payloads as JSON so they can be replayed, inspected, and delivered across adapters.
impact: Functions, Maps, Sets, class instances, and other non-JSON values fail at runtime with PAYLOAD_NOT_JSON.

fixes.title: Pass JSON data
fixes.description: Replace the payload with plain JSON data, or store complex data elsewhere and pass a reference.

title: Media capability is unsupported
description: Resolved adapter and model capability evidence proves that the authored media operation, modality, or option is unsupported.
rationale: Conclusive capability mismatches should fail during review instead of at provider I/O.
impact: The authored model operation will fail before producing a usable media result.

fixes.title: Choose a supported capability
fixes.description: Use an adapter/model that supports the authored operation and modalities, or remove the unsupported option.

title: Provider file belongs to another adapter
description: Resolved source evidence identifies a provider-file asset passed to a different provider adapter.
rationale: Provider file identifiers are scoped to the provider that created them.
impact: The destination provider cannot read the file and the model call will fail.

fixes.title: Hydrate or upload the file
fixes.description: Hydrate the asset and upload it through the destination provider before invoking the media operation.

title: AssetRef is not hydrated
description: Resolved source evidence proves an opaque AssetRef is passed directly to a model operation.
rationale: AssetRef is a persistence reference, not model-readable media.
impact: The model cannot consume the reference and the operation will fail before provider I/O.

fixes.title: Hydrate the asset
fixes.description: Call the owning AssetStore get operation and pass the resulting Asset to the model.

title: Media ingest has no text derivation
description: Indexed media ingest evidence has no required describe or transcribe derivation binding.
rationale: Retrieval requires derived text for media that is not directly searchable.
impact: The ingested media may be stored without searchable semantic content.

fixes.title: Bind a derivation
fixes.description: Attach an explicit describe or transcribe operation to the media ingest source.

title: Derived media text loses attribution
description: Available page or time attribution is not preserved on derived searchable text.
rationale: Attribution connects retrieved text to the source frame that supports it.
impact: Retrieved evidence cannot be traced back to its page or time range.

fixes.title: Preserve attribution
fixes.description: Carry available page or time attribution from the ingest derivation into indexed text records.

title: Media output is discarded
description: A proven media output is bound while canonical content and messages are unread in the compiler-visible module graph.
rationale: Generated media is useful only when the canonical result is consumed or persisted explicitly.
impact: The operation spends provider time and cost but its media result is lost.

fixes.title: Consume the result
fixes.description: Read content or messages, or explicitly persist the generated Asset with an AssetStore.

title: Raw media is routed to retained metadata
description: Resolved architecture evidence proves raw media is explicitly routed to observability or vector metadata.
rationale: Ordinary observability and vector metadata must retain bounded descriptors rather than media payloads.
impact: Raw media or bearer references may leak into durable telemetry or retrieval metadata.

fixes.title: Store a safe descriptor
fixes.description: Remove raw media from retained metadata and project only bounded modality, size, and MIME facts.

title: Evidence kind is invalid
description: A canonical evidence.record call uses a literal kind outside the bounded evidence-kind contract.
rationale: Inline application evidence requires a valid custom.* kind; references may use canonical or custom kinds.
impact: Runtime evidence authoring rejects this call before collector mutation.

fixes.title: Use a valid evidence kind
fixes.description: Use a bounded custom.* kind for inline data or a canonical kind for an existing artifact reference.

title: Canonical evidence kind is reserved
description: A canonical evidence.record call uses a reserved canonical artifact kind for inline evidence.
rationale: Canonical artifact kinds describe Crux-owned sources; inline application evidence must use custom.*.
impact: Runtime evidence authoring rejects this call before collector mutation.

fixes.title: Use a custom kind
fixes.description: Rename the inline evidence kind to a bounded custom.* value.

title: Embedding does not support the authored modality
description: Resolved embedding and consumer-call evidence proves that media input uses a modality the dense embedding does not declare.
rationale: A text-only or narrower embedding cannot produce comparable vectors for unsupported media.
impact: The embedding, indexing, knowledge-base, or retrieval call will fail before producing a usable vector.

fixes.title: Choose a compatible embedding
fixes.description: Use an embedding that declares the authored modality, or pass text input instead.

title: Namespace uses incompatible embedding identities
description: Resolved consumers share a namespace and vector storage but use different exact dense or sparse embedding identities.
rationale: Similarity search is meaningful only when every vector in a namespace belongs to one embedding space.
impact: Indexing or retrieval will reject the mixed space, or an existing mixed store will fail loudly at search time.

fixes.title: Align the namespace embedding
fixes.description: Use matching dense and sparse embedding identities for the namespace, or choose a distinct namespace.

title: Sparse embedding is combined with media
description: Resolved source evidence proves that media is declared, embedded, queried, or indexed through a sparse-only branch.
rationale: Sparse embeddings are text-only and cannot make media chunks searchable.
impact: The media input cannot produce a sparse vector and sparse-only indexed media is unreachable.

fixes.title: Use a dense media embedding
fixes.description: Route media through a compatible dense embedding and reserve sparse embeddings for text.

title: Prompt declares multiple history projections
description: A prompt may declare one canonical history projection through history() or history.recent().
rationale: One projection must own causal grouping and model-facing history selection.
impact: Multiple projections make history ownership and request planning ambiguous.

fixes.title: Keep one history projection
fixes.description: Remove all but one history() or history.recent() entry from the prompt use array.

title: Representation wrappers are ordered incorrectly
description: Representation ladders must follow prefer, summarizable, offloadable, then outermost droppable order.
rationale: A monotonic wrapper order gives every contributor one unambiguous degradation path.
impact: Invalid topology can weaken capability ownership or fail request composition before dispatch.

fixes.title: Reorder the representation ladder
fixes.description: Use each non-terminal wrapper at most once and make droppable the outermost wrapper.

title: Signal provider identity is not stable
description: Executable Signal providers require a statically proven non-empty string id so generated Runtime programs can import stable provider authority.
rationale: Executable Signal providers require a statically proven non-empty string id so generated Runtime programs can import stable provider authority.
impact: A missing or dynamic provider id cannot be pinned into the generated Runtime program and fails before managed-transport drain.

fixes.description: Pass a direct string literal to signalProvider({ id }).
fixes.title: Use a stable provider id

title: Managed transport binding contains a live value
description: RuntimeManagedTransportBinding declarations are inert and secret-free. They must not author Request, client, credential, socket, callback, handle, or onEvent fields.
rationale: RuntimeManagedTransportBinding declarations are inert and secret-free. They must not author Request, client, credential, socket, callback, handle, or onEvent fields.
impact: Live values in bindings are rejected by Runtime validation and must never enter generated program manifests.

fixes.description: Remove live Request, client, credential, socket, callback, handle, and onEvent fields from managedTransportBinding() options.
fixes.title: Keep the binding inert

title: Managed transport binding identity is not stable
description: Inert managed-transport bindings require static binding id, configRef, Signal target, and provider authority so generated Runtime programs can validate them.
rationale: Inert managed-transport bindings require static binding id, configRef, Signal target, and provider authority so generated Runtime programs can validate them.
impact: A partial binding cannot be imported into the sole generated Runtime program or validated before worker start.

fixes.description: Pass literal id, configRef, and signalId values and bind an authored signalProvider().
fixes.title: Use a stable inert binding
